processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five different alloys were synthesized in one operation using five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace; each was filled from a 4-kg ingot, and the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10 × 50 × 130 mm³-sized blocks were hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.

processing_steps.method: cutting perpendicular to the rolling direction
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cut into sets of nine segments with dimensions 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Scales were removed from the surfaces after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

structures.overall_structure: fully recrystallized austenitic matrix containing nm-sized κ-carbide precipitates formed during aging

precipitates.type: κ-carbide (L'1_2-type ordered fcc carbide, approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)3AlC)
precipitates.coherency: lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to the austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix

phase_interfaces.coherence: lattice mismatch below 3% with the austenitic matrix (enables cuboidal nanoprecipitates)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Orowan bypassing of longitudinal κ-carbide rods and subsequent expansion of dislocation loops, assisted by dislocation cross-slip and, to a minor extent, shearing of κ-carbides.

interfaces.slip_behavior: After aging at 500–600 °C, twinning is reduced and strain hardening is essentially associated with κ-carbide and solid-solution strengthening.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Aging Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al for 24 h raises YS, UTS, and hardness to about twice the as-homogenized state while drastically reducing ductility; intermediate 2–6 wt.% Al variants are much less affected by aging.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements per material state
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical property screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al aged 500 °C 24 h has total elongation near 10%.

characterization_methods.purpose: hardness screening as a function of Al content and aging condition
characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness is nearly flat (~200 HBW) up to 6Al and rises steeply toward ~375 HBW at 8Al (highest curve 550 °C, 24 h).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.purpose: checking for cracks, pores, macrosegregations, and assessing the recrystallized grain structure
characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; hot rolling and water quenching resulted in a fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: Aging Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al for 24 h further increases YS, UTS, and hardness to levels twice as high as in the as-homogenized state and drastically reduces ductility [b0024].
The pronounced strengthening of the ~8 wt.% Al variant during aging is attributed to the formation of nm-sized κ-carbides [b0025].
Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al is the material with the highest Al content and lowest density among the investigated Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl set [b0024].
